title: Ordinal arithmetic: addition, multiplication, and examples
summary: Adding consecutive orders and arranging repeated blocks explains the arithmetic of ordinals.
abstract: Ordinal arithmetic describes how to join well-ordered arrangements, orders in which every nonempty selection has a first element. Addition places one arrangement after another, and multiplication repeats an arrangement in consecutive blocks. The resulting order depends on which part comes first: one point before the natural numbers leaves their order unchanged, while one point after them creates a last point. Grouping sums or products differently preserves the order, but reversing their factors can change it. These distinctions remain visible even when all the sets involved are countably infinite.
